observations.explanation: Page 3 explicitly lays out the four principles—simple actions, efficient actions, informative feedback, and guardrails—and relates them to the interface design and ablations.

Pages 5–7 report SWE-agent results against the tested baselines and Lite ablations; for example, page 6 shows 18.0% resolved versus 11.0% for the shell-only agent on SWE-bench Lite, with several ablations performing worse than the full interface.

Page 5 says the results, ablations, and analysis use two models. The paper does report results with both GPT-4 Turbo and Claude 3 Opus (pages 2 and 6), but does not establish transfer to additional model families.
Page 8 reports from manual inspection that agents rarely deviate from the repeated edit-and-test pattern and rarely recognize dead ends or reset their approach.
